title: allow to disable suspend inhibitiors per activity
line: An activity can now be set to sleep on schedule even when apps ask to keep the computer awake.
explanation: Per-activity power settings could only add inhibitions (keep the screen on, don't sleep); there was no way to make an activity ignore the sleep inhibitions that apps such as media players register, so one app could keep the machine awake all night. Powerdevil now has an activity setting IgnoreAppSuspendInhibitions: while that activity is current, apps' requests no longer stop automatic sleep (they still keep the screen on), and the Activities settings page gets an "Apps preventing sleep" checkbox under "While on this activity, allow:" to turn it off.

commits.message:
daemon: allow activities to ignore apps' sleep inhibitions

An activity could only add its own inhibitions, so an app asking to keep
the system awake always kept it from sleeping, even in an activity meant
to sleep after a while. Activities can now ignore apps' sleep requests.

BUG: 345115

kcms/activities: add option to ignore apps preventing sleep

Apps that ask to keep the system awake always stopped it from sleeping,
with no way to opt out per activity. A new "Apps preventing sleep" box
lets an activity ignore those requests when it allows sleeping itself.

BUG: 345115

media.caption: Activity settings on master: only the activity's own screen and sleep switches, nothing about apps.
New "Apps preventing sleep" box (unchecked here = ignore them); it is greyed out when the activity itself blocks sleep or screen off.
Master, idle action set to fire after 60 s, an app holding a keep-awake inhibition: 85 s idle and nothing happens.
With the box unchecked, same app inhibition: the idle action fires at 61 s (logout prompt used as a safe stand-in for sleep on the rig).
